analysis:
Both units are base-side text of docs/architecture/inference.md. The PR patch is documentation only: the scheduler/loop configuration table at about lines 1087-1090 (head) is rewritten to describe prefill chunk/step geometry (2048/4096 for Gemma 4, 512/2048 otherwise), the solo stripe, and a bidirectionalMediaPrefillChunkCeiling of 512. The head-side ranges 1101-1148 and 2030-2047 are outside the supplied excerpts, so I did not review those additions.

No code, key handling, attestation, authorization or encryption paths change in what I saw, and the prose does not alter any retained control. Possibly relevant threats are T-041 (prefix-cache oracle), T-010 and T-029 (DoS and resource use), and TB-007.

The documented default of a 2048-token prefill chunk for Gemma 4 could affect TTFT timing and per-step GPU occupancy. It does not change cache scoping, HMAC lookup naming, the TTL or the SEC-035 accepted risk. A doc-only change gives no evidence of a regression, and the threat model's cache-oracle description is not invalidated by the visible text.

Remaining questions for integration: whether the unseen head hunks (including the new content near lines 1101-1148 and 2030-2047) make claims about security controls that diverge from the canonical threat model. The code in EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift (prefillGeometry) is not supplied, so doc-to-code accuracy is unverified. The threat-model files may need review if the doc states security properties.
